sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill for a Rockford house?
sections.html:
The Winnebago County Treasurer sends and collects the bill, and the Winnebago County Supervisor of Assessments sets the assessment behind it. Rockford is the county seat of Winnebago County, so both offices sit in the County Administration Building at 404 Elm Street in downtown Rockford. A small part of the city extends into Ogle County, so a parcel on that edge is billed by Ogle County instead.

  • Treasurer: Room 205, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., phone (815) 319-4400. Bills, payments, and the annual tax sale.
  • Supervisor of Assessments: Room 301, same hours, phone (815) 319-4460. Assessment notices, homestead exemptions, and the Board of Review.
  • County Clerk: Room 101, phone (815) 319-4253. Back taxes that were sold at tax sale, and the tax rates themselves.

A Rockford bill lists several taxing bodies on one statement: the county, the city, the park district, the library, the airport authority, Rockford Public Schools District 205 and Community College 511. Your own total depends on which tax code your parcel falls in, and the tax code is printed on the bill.

sections.h2: When were the 2025 taxes due, and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
Bills for tax year 2025 went out in early May 2026, with installments due June 12 and September 11, 2026. A late installment picks up a penalty of 1.5% per month, and the treasurer says partial payments are not accepted.

The treasurer set Friday, December 4, 2026 as the last day to pay 2025 taxes before they go to the annual tax sale, provided there are no prior-year delinquent taxes on the parcel. Payments had to reach the office or be made online by that day, and postmarks were not accepted on it.

  • E-check payments online are free.
  • Debit and credit cards carry a 2.25% fee that goes to the payment servicer, not the county.
  • The county's post office box closed in 2024. Mail checks to the Room 205 street address.
  • A returned check costs $35. Mortgage and title companies without the original bill pay a $3 duplicate bill fee per parcel.

Taxes from 2024 and earlier cannot be paid on the treasurer's website. Those go through the County Clerk at the number above, because a tax buyer has usually already paid them.

sections.h2: What is the property tax rate in Rockford?
sections.html:
For the 2024 tax year, the county's rate report shows a combined rate of 9.4764 for tax code 001, which covers a typical parcel inside the City of Rockford and Rockford School District 205. Parcels in other tax codes have different totals, for example 8.3297 for a code that pairs Rockford Park District with Harlem School District 122 and a different library district.

If your parcel sits in the East Side TIF district, the bill shows a separate TIF line. Money collected on the growth in value inside that district stays inside the district.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Rockford assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the township assessor, then file a complaint with the Winnebago County Board of Review within 30 calendar days after your township's assessments are published. The Board's page describes a four-step path: township assessor, Board of Review, the state Property Tax Appeal Board, and then court.

The 2026 schedule for Rockford Township, as posted by the Board of Review, has already run its course:

  • Assessments went online July 31, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. and notices were mailed August 3.
  • Publication was August 5, and the complaint deadline was September 4.
  • Extra evidence was due September 29 for reductions under $100,000 and October 14 for larger requests.

Cherry Valley, Durand, Laona and Owen townships share these dates, while Harlem and Roscoe ran one day later. The Board asks owners to check its page in mid-July each year for the new dates. An owner unhappy with the Board's decision has 30 days from that decision, by postmark, to go to the Property Tax Appeal Board.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and relief programs reduce a Rockford bill?
sections.html:
Winnebago County lists three programs aimed at older homeowners, in addition to the general homestead exemption that every owner-occupant should see on the bill.

  • Senior Citizen Exemption: for owners 65 or older during the assessment year who live in the home on January 1. It lowers the equalized assessed value by $5,000, and the filing deadline is December 31 of the assessment year.
  • Senior Citizen Assessment Freeze: freezes the equalized assessed value while the owner stays eligible. The treasurer's page gives a household income limit of $65,000 and requires the application before July 1.
  • Senior Citizen Tax Deferral: for owners 65 or older with household income of $75,000 or less. The state pays the deferred tax, up to $7,500 per year, and it is repaid with interest when the property sells or the estate settles. Filing deadline is March 1.

That last point matters to a seller, because the county states that repayment with interest falls due on sale of the property or settlement of the estate. The Supervisor of Assessments has also posted a notice that online claims of a nationwide property tax freeze or a federal October 15 filing date are false.

sections.h2: What happens if Rockford property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
The county sells the unpaid tax, not the house. Registered buyers bid at a live auction in the form of an interest rate, capped at 9%, and the lowest bid wins. The buyer pays the bill to the county, and the owner then deals with the County Clerk to redeem.

The treasurer's pages describe the redemption window in two ways, and both cite 35 ILCS 200/21-350: a 2.5-year period on one page and three years on another, with one year for vacant non-farm land, buildings of seven or more units, and commercial or industrial property. The certificate holder may extend the period, and interest rises over time. Ask the County Clerk for the exact deadline and payoff on your certificate before you plan a sale around it. Redemption requires cash, a money order, or a cashier's check for the exact amount.

If the tax is never redeemed, the buyer can petition the court for a tax deed. Ask your title company how a sold tax will be handled at closing, and get the redemption figure from the clerk first.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Rockford itself?
sections.html:
Rockford is the fifth-largest city in Illinois, about 90 miles west-northwest of downtown Chicago on the Rock River. The Census Bureau counted 147,384 residents in July 2025, down from 148,655 at the 2020 census, and it lists 61,324 households with a median household income of $54,752 for 2020 to 2024.

Housing is where Rockford differs most from the Chicago suburbs. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $129,000, only 54.9% of homes are owner-occupied, and median gross rent is $985. With nearly half of households renting, a lot of houses here are investor-held or former rentals.

The city began as Midway in the 1830s and grew on reapers, furniture and fasteners. Today manufacturing includes automotive parts and aerospace, alongside a larger health care sector. Neighborhoods on the near east side were hit by Keith Creek flooding in 2006 and 2007, and a July 2024 flood overwhelmed the city's stormwater systems. The airport averages about 37 inches of snow a year, and spring storms bring hail and strong winds, which puts roofs and drainage in focus.

sections.h2: Do Rockford landlords have to register a rental before selling?
sections.html:
Yes, any residential rental property inside city limits must be on the City of Rockford's rental registry, which also covers short-term rentals. The registry came out of the Residential Quality Support Ordinance. Fines of $50 to $750 per day per property can be imposed for failing to register, and the system is free to use.

Registration asks for the property address, number of dwelling units, and contact details for the owner, manager and tenant. Registered owners get emails when police or fire respond to the property and before a code enforcement inspection.

An owner selling a tenant-occupied house should confirm the registration is current before listing.

sections.h2: How should I handle the tax bill when selling a Rockford house?
sections.html:
Ask the treasurer for the exact amount due on your parcel number, ask the County Clerk whether any year has been sold, and give both figures to the closing agent or title company.

  • Pull the 2025 bill and the parcel number.
  • Confirm the exemptions on the bill are yours. A senior deferral or freeze affects the payoff.
  • Ask the County Clerk about tax years 2024 and earlier if any bill looks unpaid.
  • Check the rental registry status if the house has had tenants.

If repairs or back taxes make a traditional listing hard, an as-is cash buyer is one route, and the title company can pay the tax from the proceeds.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Rockford property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Winnebago County Treasurer at 404 Elm Street, Room 205, online, or by phone. Checks and e-checks are free, while cards carry a 2.25% fee. Many local banks and credit unions also take payments with your bill in hand.

faqs.q: What is the Rockford property tax penalty for paying late?
faqs.a: The penalty is 1.5% per month on each late installment, per the Winnebago County Treasurer. The treasurer adds that penalties change every 30 days and that partial payments are not accepted. Use the county's online payment page for the amount including penalty.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my Rockford assessment for 2026?
faqs.a: No, the Rockford Township complaint deadline for 2026 was September 4. The next window opens when assessments are published, normally late July or early August, and runs 30 calendar days. Contact the township assessor before then, since an informal correction is possible earlier in the year.

faqs.q: Is Rockford in Winnebago County or Ogle County?
faqs.a: Rockford is mostly in Winnebago County and serves as its county seat, but a portion of the city extends into Ogle County. A parcel in that Ogle portion is billed by Ogle County. Check the county named on your tax bill.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Rockford house with back taxes owed?
faqs.a: Yes, a house with back taxes can be sold, and the title company can pay the tax from the proceeds at closing. If the tax was sold to a buyer, get a redemption figure from the Winnebago County Clerk at (815) 319-4253. Redemption has to be made in certified funds or cash.
